A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MicroG-4M and MicroG-Bench, with readily matched methods, datasets, figures, and experiments. Text and visual material are readable throughout. The supplied v1.pdf ends with references; v3.pdf additionally contains Appendices A–F.

before.justification: Tables 1–4 report original action-recognition, video-captioning, and VQA evaluations on MicroG-4M. Figure 3 provides qualitative model comparisons.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, supplemented by JHMDB transfer results, Tarsier2 evaluations, and qualitative and per-class results in the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the collection, tracking, and annotation pipeline, with no established architecture change. However, v3 Appendix C says LLMs only polish manually generated annotations, contradicting both versions' Section 3 account of LLM-generated and ranked QA candidates. These conflicting accounts prevent reliably determining whether the QA-construction procedure changed.

E1.justification: v3 adds terrestrial HAR evaluation on JHMDB Split 1 as a contrast to MicroG-4M transfer (Section 5.1, Table 3). The MicroG-4M corpus and three tasks remain unchanged. Other datasets in Table 10 provide contextual statistics, not additional model-evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Tarsier2-Recap-7B is added to both captioning and VQA comparisons in v3 Tables 4–5; all previous table comparators remain. The additional HAR qualitative comparison in Figure 4 includes I3D NLN alongside the Slow models, expanding the comparator set used for qualitative analysis.

E3.justification: The added transfer comparison specifies matched AVA fine-tuning, zero-shot JHMDB Split 1 evaluation, and overlapping actions. Tarsier2 evaluations use 16 input frames. Existing splits, metrics, and model configurations are retained; Appendix F.1 newly explains the existing split-construction procedure rather than reporting a revised split.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands diagnostic analysis through the terrestrial transfer contrast, per-class AP breakdowns in Figures 7–8, and additional HAR, captioning, and VQA cases in Figures 4–6. These examine action confusions, missing contextual details, occlusion, location identification, and hallucination. The original Figure 3 analysis remains.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or experimental error bars. The new per-class AP bar charts describe differences across action classes, not uncertainty across runs.

E6.justification: Original benchmark scores are retained. New results include JHMDB mAP of 47.50 for SlowFast and 34.24 for Slow, Tarsier2 captioning S-BERT of 51.35 and VQA S-VQA of 29.60, and extensive class-level and qualitative outcomes. Section 4 also changes Person Interaction/Movement counts from 1,198/1,037 to 4,288/3,987; this establishes revised reported statistics, not a changed corpus.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theory or proofs. The added QA-density arithmetic and discussion of long-tailed class frequencies do not introduce substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: the first unified microgravity dataset and benchmark covering HAR, captioning, and VQA, exposing weaknesses of terrestrial models. Changing the expansion of '4M' from 'Multi-domain' to 'Multi-source' clarifies the existing real/cinematic composition without materially redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds specific limitations concerning annotation subjectivity and three-second temporal context, beyond v1's RGB, source-bias, and scale caveats. Appendices B–C clarify research-only applicability, while Appendix F.4 explains QA-density choices and cautions against interpreting density as difficulty. Section 5.2 newly interprets the JHMDB contrast as isolating a physics-driven gap.

D1.justification: Appendices E–F newly document the AVA-compatible frame-indexed format, metadata fields, bounding-box coordinates, video naming, class-coverage-based split construction, and complete action-ID mapping. Appendix C adds noncommercial research-use guidance. These substantially expand documentation for using the existing dataset, although training hyperparameters and hardware remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for JHMDB, Tarsier2, and additional VQA corpora, with Appendix F.4 positioning MicroG-4M through annotation density and scope. It removes the astronaut-identification discussion and Ali et al. (2022) reference. The main research positioning remains intact; conversion to author–year citations is stylistic.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose remain. Localized rewrites clarify microgravity motion, taxonomy adaptation, related work, and transfer analysis; terminology and acknowledgments also change. Limitations move into an expanded appendix, with additional appendix sections organizing the supplementary material rather than broadly restructuring the main narrative.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 retain identical images, with Figure 2 relocated. v3 adds qualitative panels, per-class plots, and transfer and dataset-comparison tables, substantially expanding the visual presentation. Some appendix tables redisplay existing split or distribution information. Existing benchmark tables are reformatted and extended, and the document adopts different typography and layout.

improvement.justification: The JHMDB contrast adds useful context missing from v1's transfer evidence, while per-class results, failure examples, metadata, and explicit limitations improve diagnosis and dataset usability. The net gain is limited by new inconsistencies: Appendix C contradicts Section 3 about QA provenance, supplementary counts disagree, and the claim of isolating gravity exceeds what the reported cross-dataset control establishes. These issues temper the benefits without eliminating them.
